articleTitle: A direct ac to ac frequency converter suitable for variable speed induction motor drives
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The provision of variable frequency and voltage from a fixed frequency and constant voltage supply by the combination of two solid state switching converters is described. No intermediate dc link is employed and it is shown that the output voltage and supply currents contain no harmonic components below 300 Hz in a 6-step system. The converters are force-commutated and bi-directional and therefore capable of direct regeneration to the supply. Frequency is continuously variable from zero to a value which is only limited by the switch and motor losses. The results of a numerical analysis performed on a 3,5 kW, 3-phase induction motor when fed from the output of this converter, are described. It appears that the energy stored in the leakage reactance is usefully added to the output of the machine during the ‘free wheel’ period when the phases are commutated to produce a frequency change.

articleTitle: Electrical energy supply in conurbation areas as demonstrated by West Berlin
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The steadily rising demand for electrical energy in the industrialized countries and in industrial areas continuously poses new problems which can only be solved by maximum effort in the engineering sector. This applies particularly to the power supply of conurbation areas, where the no less difficult problems of power distribution are now being added to the well-known problems of power generation. The purpose of this paper is to deal with the special aspects of power supply in conurbation areas. I will therefore start by outlining the present situation and its problems, follow up by describing the major technical facilities available to solve these problems and close by presenting a fully up-to-date concept for a conurbation area by reference to West Berlin.

articleTitle: Inverter drive system for a battery car
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Since an electronic inverter is not far removed from the ‘chopper’ modulated dc voltage controller, it has bean suggested that the dc motor be replaced by an ac machine in a battery vehicle. The advantage of using a more robust and cheaper motor hat to be weighed against an increase in the complexity and cost of the additional electronic equipment. It may also be possible to achieve a better motor characteristic with respect to the requirements of the drive. A system is described which employs a synchronous motor driven by a transistorized inverter. The experimental results of the combination show a promising torque-speed characteristic with a large starting torque provided armature reaction is reduced. The inverter is arranged to incorporate voltage control so that the motor may be operated at maximum flux per pole over its entire speed range. The results show that it is necessary to control voltage and internal angle to retain the advantages of the system.

articleTitle: Overvoltage surge phenomena on the 3 kV dc overhead track equipment of the South African railways
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In an effort to clarify certain problems being experienced on the electrified sections of the South African Railways, an automatic surge recording station was installed at Olifantsfontein on the main line between Pretoria and Johannesburg. This station served to measure and record any transient overvoltages in the section and to correlate these with lightning activity in the area. Data was accumulated over a three-year period of measurement and the results presented in the paper are considered to be representative of what might be anticipated in a severe lightning season. Although the resultant analysis indicates that the system may be adequately protected as far as overvoltages are concerned, the observed oscillatory nature of the surges could be a potential hazard to the system insulation and it is possible that further investigations may be required.

articleTitle: Technology in ground transport twenty-fifth bernard price memorial lecture
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The demand created by market forces for improved and for new products, once recognised leads to the movement of designers and engineers, attracted by the technical problems arising out of the new opportunities, This flow of skilled people is a potent factor in a competitive situation and can result in an over-swing condition in which the donor industry is denuded of staff below the level that commercial considerations alone would dictate. It may be argued that this phenomenon of technical imbalance is evident in ground transport technology when one examines the interplay between road and rail transport. The paper accepts this proposition in relation to ground transport and proceeds to describe recent work in British Rail (BR) that goes some way to restoring a proper relativity between road and rail technology. This work is believed to be of value, not only because it benefits an important industry, but also because it helps to establish a real perspective with which to view the future of ground transport and the contributions each of the two major modes might make in the next decade or so. Energy economy and the reduction of pollution are recent considerations which must modify the conventional market pressures in determining the developing roles for the different forms of ground transport and emphasises the need for a factual basis of assessment and planning. The arguments in the paper add force to the truism that road and rail are complementary modes of transport and there is a widespread need for an integrated transport policy that recognises this basic fact. The paper identifies a deficiency in the ground transport spectrum, namely the Urban Car, i.e., a free-running road vehicle designed specifically for use in and near cities.

articleTitle: Development and characteristics of a dissipative electronic le Blanc cascade for variable speed ac drives using 22 kW wound rotor machines
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A simple, reliable, robust and Accurately controllable (0,2 per cent) variable speed drive using a resistively loaded electronic rotor chopper circuit has been developed. The general system concepts, the models used for a first order analysis and design, the power electronic circuit, the information electronic subsystem and the actually realized system are all briefly discussed. It is shown that a simple two pole approach to the system leads to acceptable controller design, while the simple Tröger chopper circuit yields a very reliable force commutated chopper. The system operates reliably from standstill up to maximum speed (1 45D/r/min) at full load torque and is applicable to variable speed drives such as cranes, extruder drives, pump drives and other variable speed process drives. Work continues on the further dynamic characterization of the system, the influence of harmonic interference torques and extensions of operation to the over-synchronous, reversing and braking regions.

articleTitle: Water and the developing African state
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper is intended to be a provocative contribution to discussion of the desirability of defining and promoting the kinds of technology that might be appropriate to developing countries in Africa. The paper, which has specific reference to water, has been allocated to the seminar on Material potential; it is well at the outset, therefore, to recognise that Africa's water potential is enormous. Of all the continents, Africa possesses, for instance, by far the greatest hydro-power potential — roughly equal to that of North and South America together. Of the area south of the Sahara, it is only in some parts of South Africa, SWA/Namibia, Botswana and Rhodesia that extensive dry regions are encountered. The vast potential of the remainder lies largely untapped, through reluctance on the part of the rest of Southern Africa to take advantage of the available markets for water and electricity because they happen to be in South Africa.

articleTitle: Thyristor converters/inverters for controlling dc and ac motors — which drive system is most suitable for the job?
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The enthusiasm and resourcefulness shown by thyristor circuit and conversion equipment designers in recent years has led to an abundance of motor control systems. Thyristor converters for armature and field control of dc motors, forced and naturally commutated inverters for ac motor control, slip power recovery systems for induction motors, cyclo-converters etc, are all available and offer a wide variation in performance capabilities. This must be very confusing to the ultimate user whose practical knowledge of the many systems is conceivably limited. It is the intention of this paper to overcome this confusion by presenting the technical performance of these systems in a clear way based on the extensive experience now available. The performance available from these schemes is not only dependent on which system is chosen but also on the method used to control the system. For example, either armature or field reversal can be used to cause a dc motor to regenerate, these two methods will produce different performance results. Also, the performance of an inverter motor drive will be significantly changed if pulse width modulation is employed rather than the more conventional square wave control. This paper will therefore also consider those control methods relevant to the performance of these systems. Each system will be briefly described and its performance characteristics and limitations clearly explained with particular reference to comparisons between the systems. The paper will conclude with a brief statement of future trends in this continuously expanding field of conversion equipment.
